content.comment_body: Dear Experts, In the [product_name] manual, I found the following note: You can only substitute two [product_name] modules ([article_no]) with one [product_name] module ([article_no]) if using a 24 VDC power supply. Similarly, you can only substitute two [product_name] modules ([article_no]) with one [product_name] module ([article_no]) if DC and positive-voltage input are used. I'm unclear on whether this means the substitution can't be reversed (e.g., swapping one [product_name] module for two [product_name] modules)? Or does it imply that if there are four [product_name] modules, we can't perform another substitution after replacing the first two with the larger module?

To answer the first question: This means that if the power supply for two [product_name] modules ([article_no]) is 12 VDC, substitution with a [product_name] module ([article_no]) isn't possible since it requires 24 VDC. If those two modules are supplied with 24 VDC, replacement is permitted. Regarding the second question: The [product_name] ([article_no]) can operate with +24 VDC, -24 VDC, or 24 VAC, but the [product_name] ([article_no]) is limited to 24 VDC supply. If the [product_name] modules use either -24 VDC or 24 VAC, it's not possible to replace them with the [product_name] module. Check the technical specifications of the expansion modules found at the end of the manual.
Thank you, that's now clear and well explained!
